asset.label: Orlando 1928 bungalow
asset.framing: Renting must earn the right to beat selling.
asset.emotional_note: Real attachment. The model exists so nostalgia does not override the math - and so the math does not pretend the attachment is worthless.

lean_note: Lane increasingly leans toward selling. The decision is NOT final and the model must not close it early.

mortgage.amortization_note: Derived planning calculation (~28.2 years), not a substitute for the contractual maturity date.

branches.label: Sell
case_for: Lane strongly dislikes living through constant showings
Clean break reduces cognitive and logistical load

branches.label: Rent
case_for: Tenant offsets a meaningful portion of carrying cost
Allows a later sale while vacant
case_against: Not naturally cash-flow positive under the current mortgage
A large landlord reserve ties up capital

branches.label: Temporarily hold / defer
case_for: Removes a decision from the compressed move window
case_against: Full carrying cost with no offset for every deferred month

strategies.label: Clean exit
strategies.target: Under contract in roughly 2-3 weeks without giving the property away.

strategies.label: Maximum reasonable proceeds
strategies.target: Price and strategy assuming roughly 30-45 days of market exposure.

collect_per_strategy: what happens with no offer by day 7 / 14 / 21
remote management after Lane leaves Florida
preferred_sequence: Lane + Klein + Tilly drive the Tundra west
sale_workstream.sequence_note: Temporary overlap between California rent and the Orlando mortgage may be rational if it substantially reduces stress and improves sale execution. That is a deliberate purchase of calm, not a mistake.

property_management_workstream.compare_on: Net owner distribution, not the highest promised rent.

baseline_items: electrical GFCI / open neutral / exposed wiring / weatherproofing

hvac.documentation: Major equipment and warranty paperwork assembled.
hvac.unresolved: Permit / final municipal mechanical inspection approval proof.
hvac.rule: A permitting agreement is not proof that a permit was closed and finaled.
